initial_control_scope.outer_source_topology: Fresh Clojure Compiler.eval splits an outer top-level do, so source `(do (eval '(def x ...)) ... (var x))` can admit x before later compilation. Session::eval_with_macros prepares its entire source input before runtime; an unresolved direct var in that same already-being-prepared input fails before eval executes. Both original topology failures are retained. Public eval of the equivalent do form itself compiles its ordered units and passes in both phases. The moved-inner control is not counted as fixing outer source semantics.
initial_control_scope.scope_conclusion: This source-entry distinction is not an actionable regression in the public form-data eval consumer. Accepted design7 specifies incremental input compilation and no binding changes on a compile error; docs/runtime/compiled-repl-macros.md specifies failed input compilation publishes no Runtime input bindings. The unchanged script_compile_failure_preserves_existing_runtime_bindings regression enforces whole source preparation (`(def keep99) unresolved` retains17). #515 requires compilation units within the form passed to ordinary public eval and persistent state for subsequent prepared inputs/lookups, which are satisfied. Broadening ordinary source preparation to JVM Compiler.eval top-level unit timing would alter established source atomicity and is separate from this binding.
